facts.claim: Run with npx from the vendor package @playwright/mcp, pinned to the current npm version 0.0.83, with headless, isolated and block-service-workers flags
facts.evidence: dist-tags.latest is 0.0.83 (published 2026-09-28); the vendor README documents npx @playwright/mcp and the flags --headless, --isolated, --block-service-workers.
README requires Node.js 18 or newer; the npm registry entry for 0.0.83 has engines node >=18.

facts.claim: The package is published by the vendor's repository microsoft/playwright-mcp (Apache-2.0)
facts.evidence: Registry repository url git+https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-mcp.git, matching the README page.

facts.claim: --headless runs without a window (headed is the default); --isolated keeps the profile in memory; --block-service-workers blocks service workers
facts.evidence: "run browser in headless mode, headed by default"; "keep the browser profile in memory, do not save it to disk."

facts.claim: --allowed-origins and --blocked-origins do not affect redirects and are not a security boundary; Playwright MCP is not a security boundary
facts.evidence: "does not serve as a security boundary"

facts.claim: File access is limited to workspace roots and file:// is blocked unless --allow-unrestricted-file-access is passed
facts.evidence: "allow access to files outside of the workspace roots"

facts.claim: --no-sandbox disables the browser sandbox for all process types
facts.evidence: "disable the sandbox for all process types that are normally sandboxed."

facts.claim: Tools that navigate, run scripts, upload or save: browser_navigate, browser_evaluate, browser_run_code_unsafe, browser_file_upload, browser_pdf_save, browser_route, cookie and storage tools
facts.evidence: Tool list names these under core automation and the opt-in capability groups.

facts.claim: browser_tabs is the read-only tab tool but its action values are not spelled out, so no smoke test is set
facts.evidence: "List, create, close, or select a browser tab" with an undocumented action enum.

choices.decision: Archetype stdio-npx with the version pinned to 0.0.83
choices.because: The vendor ships a local npm package and no hosted server; the README suggests @latest, which the template avoids
No window, no saved profile; these are documented flags usable over stdio

choices.decision: Consent on navigation, script, upload, save and storage tools
choices.because: Arbitrary pages and scripts are the main risk

open: The README's 'Browser installation' section is empty: the exact browser install step and whether the server installs a browser itself were not confirmed.
The README suggests @playwright/mcp@latest; the pin 0.0.83 is an alpha-era 0.0.x release and its compatibility with older Node 18 builds was not tested.
browser_tabs action values (list, new, close, select) are not enumerated; no smoke test is set.
The README says origin allow lists are not a security boundary, so no --allowed-origins is set; whether to add one is the owner's call.
Flag descriptions come from one page (the README); the npm registry cannot confirm them.
